summary.name: Notenik
summary.one_liner: Notenik is a free, open-source Mac note-taking app that stores notes as plain text files and supports Markdown, wiki-style links, and custom fields.
use_cases: take and organize notes on a Mac
write Markdown notes with citations and math
link related notes with wiki-style links
store notes in plain text synced via cloud
generate a static website or HTML from notes
track tasks or dates with custom note fields
summary.what_it_does: Notenik is a note-taking app for the Mac that saves each note as a plain text file inside a folder, which can be placed anywhere and synced with any cloud service. Notes can be written in Markdown with support for footnotes, citations, definition lists and MathJax. Wiki-style double bracket links connect notes, and tables of contents can be generated for a single note or a whole collection. Each note has customizable fields such as Title, Body, Tags, Link, Date, Seq and Author, and collections can sort and filter by these fields. The app can also export or publish HTML in predetermined or custom designs, and can be scripted with templates and a custom URL scheme.
notable: Notes stored as plain text files in folders, editable with any text editor
Customizable per-collection fields with sorting by field
Free and open source under MIT license, source on GitHub, distributed via Mac App Store
Built-in Knowledge Base stored as a Notenik collection
caveats: Mac only; the page names no other platforms
